observation_summary: The compiler inlines object properties into local variables, but fails to account for 'delete' operations on those properties. The 'delete' operator on a local variable does not have the same effect as on an object property, leading to incorrect code generation.
hypothesis: The InlineObjectLiterals pass incorrectly assumes that object properties can be safely inlined into local variables without considering that 'delete' operations on those properties will fail or behave incorrectly when applied to the new local variables. This is a missing validation check in the optimization logic.
prediction: The fix will involve adding a check to ensure that if an object property is subject to a 'delete' operation, it is excluded from the inlining optimization.
experiment_rationale: The failure is a direct result of an optimization pass (InlineObjectLiterals) failing to validate the safety of its transformation in the presence of a specific operator ('delete'). This is a classic missing guard/validation condition.
reasoning_summary: The bug is caused by the compiler's failure to check if an object property is deleted before inlining it. This is a missing validation check (Checking) in the optimization logic. It is not an Algorithm/Method issue because the core logic of inlining is fine, just applied too broadly. It is not Assignment/Initialization because the issue is the decision to inline, not the value assigned.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The issue is not the implementation of the inlining algorithm itself, but the lack of a guard condition to prevent it from running in invalid scenarios.
